## New investigation idea

- **[2026-10-12] The 10-11 briefing lists MONY Group as a new buy and calls it a fit "with no AI link". Two weeks ago the paper-trader bought Auto Trader and wrote down the opposite: agentic AI search is the main risk for UK online portals. MONY is the most exposed of that group, because it owns no stock and no data of its own.** The briefing's Investment Opportunities section scores MONY 5/5 (MF#15, P/E 11.3, ROIC 33.6%) and treats "no AI link" as a plus, which means it only ran the AI-*bubble* test. [[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-09-30-AUTO]] names its "Key Risk" as "AI agents disintermediating classifieds". It says the whole UK classifieds group sold off on that fear, and it accepts the risk only because Auto Trader's moat is "dealer stock supply and pricing data, not the search box." A price-comparison site has the reverse setup. Its supply is insurers' and lenders' quotes, which any agent can request directly, and its traffic comes from search, the channel AI answers are replacing. A low P/E and high ROIC are what you would expect to see if the market is already pricing that in. Rightmove (RMV) sits on the same screen at 4/5, so the question will come up again. This is the practical form of the 2026-09-29 connection (the risk table has no AI-disruption test): the first new name since then went straight through the same gap. Concrete step: before acting on the MONY card, write one line answering "what does MONY own that an AI agent can't get directly from the insurer?" Use the AUTO page's moat test as the template, and check how much of MONY's revenue still comes from search referrals.

## New cross-domain connection

- **[2026-10-12] The briefing also calls EOG Resources "unrelated to AI". AI & Tech's power tracker shows why that is wrong: the biggest new demand for Texas gas is AI data centres. That makes EOG a quiet long on the same AI build-out that Fred's ORCL short and his ORCL, PLTR and NBIS puts bet against.** The 10-11 briefing proposes EOG (MF#50, first energy holding) as "USD exposure unrelated to AI". [[ai-tech/data-dc-power-construction-tracker-2026-06-25]] lists the largest permitted gas plant in US history, GW Ranch (7.7 GW, West Texas), plus NextEra's 5.2 GW Anderson County CCGT and Crusoe's behind-the-meter gas plant at Google's Armstrong County AI campus, all within reach of Texas gas basins. [[ai-tech/model-dc-power-regional-balance-2026-06-25]] adds the price link: ERCOT wholesale power up ~45% in 2026, with Henry Hub projected at $4.00 vs ~$3.10, and [[ai-tech/source-epoch-stargate-us-sites-2026]] says at least 3 of 7 Stargate sites run on on-site gas. EOG is one of the largest US gas producers, with a dry-gas play (Dorado) in South Texas (outside knowledge, worth checking against its latest 10-Q). So if the AI capex cycle cracks the way Burry's thesis and Fred's ~€1,031 of puts expect, gas demand forecasts and EOG would likely fall too. EOG would not diversify away from AI. It would partly offset the bearish hedge. The trade may still be worth doing for its value case, but it should be booked as AI-correlated. This pairs with today's MONY idea: the briefing's "AI link" field only checks for bubble exposure, so it labels a disruption victim (MONY) and an AI-demand beneficiary (EOG) the same way. Concrete fix: split the field into "AI capex demand / AI disruption / none".

## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-11] Fred's $TEST holding has had no price for six weeks, and the weekly refresh just carries the 08-27 number forward. The open question used to be "why hold it?". Now it is "can it be sold at all, and for how much?"** [[crypto/crypto-portfolio]] has shown TST at a stale $0.01755 since 2026-08-27. Every refresh since says the `test-token-tst` CoinMarketCap slug 404s and the `test-token` page shows 0 circulating supply and no market data ("preview-listing status"). Yet the Position Notes row still says "~$11M market cap, 44K holders". Today's check: the Crypto.com Exchange feed (`crypto-market-data` MCP) has no TST_USD ticker. That isn't proof of anything, since it may never have been listed there, but it is one fewer venue. The older ideas (2026-07-26 compensated-variance verdict, 2026-07-30 *Number Go Up* / fraud checklist) are about whether the thesis holds. This one comes first: a position that can't be priced may be one that can't be exited, and its value in any portfolio total is unknown. Concrete step: (1) check TST's status on Binance spot (TST/USDT was listed in Feb 2025; look for a delisting or monitoring-tag notice) and the depth of its main PancakeSwap pool on BNB Smart Chain; (2) check CoinGecko as a second price source; (3) if neither shows a live market, mark the row "unpriceable — exit route unknown" instead of carrying a stale price, and decide in one line whether to sell what can be sold. Also note: the Notes row's market-cap and holder figures are from the original clipping and should be dated or removed.

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-11] The stablecoin law that Finance's Bessent piece calls "financial repression" also bans the yield. The synthetic dollar built by the team behind Fred's $EV holding exists to sell exactly that missing yield. That makes it both the beneficiary and the regulatory target, and its 13.25% APR was clipped before the crypto winter.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-bond-market-bessent-stablecoins-2026-09-02]] argues that GENIUS Act stablecoins are a captive T-bill buyer: issuers keep the Treasury yield and holders earn ~0% while inflation runs 3–4%. The page doesn't mention that this is written into the law: GENIUS Act payment-stablecoin issuers are prohibited from paying holders interest or yield. [[crypto/company-smardex]] describes USDN, a delta-neutral synthetic dollar (vault/long split, "similar in concept to Ethena") paying 13.25% APR. That yield comes from leveraged ETH longs paying funding, not from T-bills, so USDN sits outside GENIUS reserve rules and offers what GENIUS stablecoins can't. [[crypto/company-everything-inc]] records that Everything.inc is built by the same SmarDex team, so USDN's health is a read on the team behind a token Fred holds (−71% from ATH). Two things follow. (1) **Regulation:** demand for yield-bearing dollars is the gap the Bessent piece describes. Whether exchanges and protocols may pass yield to holders has been one of the main disputes in the CLARITY Act market-structure talks, and [[crypto/source-morningstar-crypto-winter-2026-07-24]] lists CLARITY's progress as a *bullish* catalyst without saying the bill could also close this route (check the bill's current yield language before relying on this). (2) **Cycle:** delta-neutral yield depends on longs paying funding. With BTC −25% YTD and retail "rotated to AI", funding usually compresses, so the April 13.25% (clipped with the funding rate showing 0.000000%) probably isn't the current figure. Neither [[crypto/crypto-overview]]'s "Delta-neutral stablecoins" narrative row nor the DeFi watchlist's "is the APR sustainable?" question has been revisited since May. Concrete step: record USDN's current APR, supply and peg history next to the April figures on company-smardex, and add the GENIUS no-yield rule to the Bessent page's stablecoin section as the mechanism behind its repression argument.
